The mutated offsets (+0x07/+0x1C/+0x1D/+0x22) are small struct flags typical of an internal state-machine context, not actor chain keys. The target's class is in the Command/Event state-machine domain, not in the CharaBase/PlayerBase/NpcBase actor hierarchy. No new entries added to data_dependency_catalog.json.

structuralMismatch: All writes are SINGLE BYTES at offsets < 0x40. Canonical actor chain keys (CharaBase.0x60, CharaBase.0xDC.*, CharaBase.0x154/0x158, PlayerBase.0xF1, MyPlayer.0x15D-0x15F, etc.) all live at offsets >= 0x5D and are usually u16/u32 width.

The BCS-Y-0278 pure-native receivers write u32/u16 values at canonical actor offsets. The 0x0131 deep handlers write boolean state flags conditionally, in a pattern that matches a state-machine context object.

structuralConclusion: WS-G confirms the event-condition-consumer-findings pass's interim note: the target object class is in the Command/Event state-machine domain, not in the actor hierarchy. The writes at target+0x07/+0x1C/+0x1D/+0x22 are state flags managed by the EndClientOrderEvent consumer; they cannot be modeled as chain-key writes against CharaBase / PlayerBase / NpcBase because the offsets and the target class are both structurally incompatible. No N-API reader exists in the catalog that reads any actor offset matching these writes. The /loop's original '2-4 new chain-key writes' prediction is structurally false for 0x0131 just as it was for 0x012E/0x016B/0x016F: the deferred-apply receivers do not contribute per-actor chain-key writes.
